key_insight: Regularized regression, especially Ridge, can accurately identify ship manoeuvring hydrodynamic coefficients from CFD-based free-running data while reducing the multicollinearity problems that limit ordinary least squares.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable data-driven calibration of Abkowitz-type manoeuvring models for ship design, control, and simulation when experimental system-identification data are limited.
method: Train ordinary least squares and regularized regression models on URANS-generated zig-zag and turning-circle manoeuvre data.
Compare coefficient-set sizes, minimum training lengths, and manoeuvre combinations for prediction performance.
Validate synthetic training data against experimental benchmark manoeuvre results.
evidence_signal: The study reports that larger and more diverse manoeuvre datasets improve prediction, with large-angle zig-zag data particularly effective when multicollinearity is controlled and Ridge regression giving the best balance of efficiency and accuracy.
watch_item: Larger coefficient sets increase flexibility but also raise multicollinearity risk, so model selection and input-data diversity must be handled carefully.
paper_title: Regularized Machine Learning for System Identification of Ship Free-Running Manoeuvres from CFD-Based Synthetic Data: A Comparative Study
